Echinopsis pachanoi , synonyms including Trichocereus pachanoi and Trichocereus macrogonus var. pachanoi , is a fast-growing columnar cactus found in the Andes at 2,000–3,000 m (6,600–9,800 ft) in altitude. [ 3 ] [ 4 ] It is one of a number of kinds of cacti known as San Pedro cactus. It is native to Ecuador , and Peru , but is also found in Bolivia, Colombia, central Chile, the Canary Islands, and mainland Spain, [ 2 ] and  is cultivated in other parts of the world. [ 5 ] [ 6 ] Uses for it include traditional medicine and traditional veterinary medicine, and it is widely grown as an ornamental cactus. It has been used for healing and religious divination in the Andes Mountains region for over 3,000 years. [ 7 ]
